To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) CD4+ T lymphocytes that express CCR5 can produce anti-viral CCL3 and CCL4 ligands in response to activation, and 2) CD4+ lymphocytes that express and produce anti-viral CC chemokine ligands are resistant to infection by HIV-1 strains that use the CCR5 co-receptor to enter target cells.

1) individual activated primary CD4+ cells that secrete RANTES, MIP-1α or MIP-1β are self-protected against infection with R- but not X-tropic HIV-1 and 2) this protection is selective in that CD4+ cells in the same culture remain infectable with the R- but not the X-tropic virus.
“Individual CD4+ T lymphocytes that secrete anti- HIV-1 CCR5 ligand are ‘self- protected’ against infection by R5, but not X4, isolates of HIV -1.”
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which CD8+ T cells and CD4+ cells control HIV infection.
understanding the mechanisms by which the immune system controls the infection of activated primary CD4+T cells by HIV-1.
the role of CCR5 ligand expression by T cells as a potential mechanism for the protection of these cells from infection by R5 HIV- 1.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the autocrine production of anti-viral ligands by activated CD4+ lymphocytes protects these cells from R5 HIV- 1 infection, but not from infection by X4 viruses.
CD4+ T-cells that secrete anti-HIV-1 CCR5 ligand are protected by autocrine mechanisms from infection by R5 HIV- 1, but not X4 HIV-1.
the autocrine secretion of anti-virally active CCR5 ligand by individual CD4+ helper T cells can protect against R5 but not dual- or X4-tropic strains of HIV- 1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the anti-HIV activity of CD4+ T-cell-derived CCL4 is a consequence of its ability to inhibit HIV infection of the producing CD4+ T- cell.
HIV-1 infection of CD4+ T lymphocytes is prevented by a combination of paracrine and autocrine mechanisms, with autocrine mechanisms predominating.
the autocrine secretion of anti-virus CCR5 ligand protects individual CD4+T cells against R5 HIV infection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the anti-viral CCL3, CCL4, and CCL5 ligands produced by CD4+ T lymphocytes can protect these same cells against infection by HIV-1.
CD4+ T-cell-derived CCR5 ligand is an important factor in the control of HIV-1 infection and may play a role in HIV-1 latency.
the autocrine secretion of CCL3, CCL3L1, CCL4, CCL5 and CCL5L1 by individual CD4+T cells can block the replication of R5 HIV- 1, but not X4 HIV-1.
